Chest pain or pressure means discomfort, tightness, heaviness, squeezing, or burning felt in the chest. A sudden worst-ever headache is a headache that arrives abruptly, reaches severe intensity very quickly, and is unlike any headache the person has had before. It is often described as a thunderclap onset, and it may arrive with nausea, vomiting, neck stiffness, vision change, confusion, or weakness. Ordinary headaches build more gradually and follow a familiar pattern; a sudden worst-ever headache breaks that pattern, which is why it is a red-flag symptom.

Why this symptom needs urgent care

A sudden worst-ever headache needs urgent care because it can be the first sign of bleeding or pressure problems inside the head, which need same-day assessment and imaging.
